name: Jasper National Park
tagline: A wilder, quieter half of the Icefields Parkway's Rockies scenery, home to a genuine glacier you can walk on and one of the world's largest dark sky preserves.
highlight: Standing on the Athabasca Glacier's ancient ice, a river of frozen water older than any city on Earth flowing imperceptibly beneath your boots.
shortDescription: A wilder, quieter half of the Canadian Rockies, home to the walkable Athabasca Glacier, Maligne Lake's Spirit Island and one of the world's largest dark sky preserves.
metaDescription: A Jasper National Park travel guide: Maligne Lake, the Athabasca Glacier, the Jasper SkyTram, wildlife, food and how to plan a Rockies trip.
nearestAirport: Edmonton International Airport (YEG), about 4 hours by road
knownFor: Maligne Lake, the Athabasca Glacier, the Jasper SkyTram

image.alt: Spirit Island on Maligne Lake in Jasper National Park

intro: Jasper is genuinely the wilder, quieter half of the classic Rockies pairing with Banff, a larger national park with noticeably fewer crowds and a real sense of remoteness.
Its centrepiece is genuinely the Athabasca Glacier, part of the Columbia Icefield, one of the few glaciers in the world visitors can walk out onto directly.
The park is also genuinely one of the largest accessible dark sky preserves on the planet, drawing stargazers alongside the usual Rockies hikers and photographers.

whyVisit.intro: Jasper's case rests genuinely on wilder, less crowded Rockies scenery paired with a genuinely walkable glacier.

points.title: The Athabasca Glacier is genuinely walkable
points.text: One of the few glaciers anywhere visitors can step out onto directly, guided or by Ice Explorer vehicle.

points.title: It's genuinely far less crowded than Banff
points.text: A larger park with a fraction of the visitor numbers at its most famous sights.

points.title: Maligne Lake and Spirit Island are genuinely a singular sight
points.text: One of the most photographed scenes in the Canadian Rockies.

points.title: The dark skies here are genuinely exceptional
points.text: One of the world's largest accessible dark sky preserves, with regular stargazing events.

points.title: Wildlife sightings are genuinely more frequent than in Banff
points.text: Elk, bighorn sheep, and black bears are all commonly seen along the roads.

attractionsIntro: Jasper's essential sights are genuinely spread across a much larger, wilder park than Banff.

attractions.name: Maligne Lake and Spirit Island
attractions.text: Genuinely one of the most photographed scenes in the Rockies, a tiny wooded island in the middle of a long glacial lake.
attractions.tip: Genuinely only reachable by boat tour — there's no trail to Spirit Island itself.

attractions.name: The Athabasca Glacier

image.file: File:Athabasca Glacier from the valley floor, Jasper National Park, Alberta, Canada.jpg
image.alt: The Athabasca Glacier in Jasper National Park

attractions.text: Genuinely part of the Columbia Icefield, one of the largest accumulations of ice south of the Arctic Circle.
attractions.tip: Genuinely only walk on the ice with a guided tour — crevasses make independent access genuinely dangerous.

attractions.name: The Jasper SkyTram
attractions.text: Genuinely one of the highest and longest guided aerial tramways in Canada, climbing to a sweeping alpine viewpoint.
attractions.tip: Genuinely bring a warm layer — the summit sits well above the treeline.

attractions.name: Athabasca Falls

image.alt: Athabasca Falls in Jasper National Park

attractions.text: Genuinely not the tallest waterfall in the Rockies, but one of the most powerful, forcing the Athabasca River through a narrow gorge.
attractions.tip: Genuinely walk the full loop trail for multiple viewpoints over the falls and gorge.

attractions.name: Pyramid Lake

image.file: File:Pyramid lake in Jasper town, Alberta, Canada1.jpg

attractions.text: Genuinely a peaceful lake just outside Jasper town, named for the pyramid-shaped mountain reflected in its water.
attractions.tip: Genuinely an easy sunset spot, a short drive from downtown Jasper.

attractions.name: Maligne Canyon

image.alt: Maligne Canyon in Jasper National Park

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the deepest canyons in the Rockies, a limestone gorge crossed by a series of dramatic footbridges.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit in winter too, if you can — the frozen canyon walk is a completely different experience.

attractions.name: Ice Explorer vehicles on the glacier

image.file: File:Ice Explorer vehicles on the Athabasca Glacier 20240824 2.jpg
image.alt: Ice Explorer vehicles on the Athabasca Glacier

attractions.text: Genuinely a unique way to reach the glacier's surface, giant all-terrain buses built specifically for the ice.
attractions.tip: Genuinely combine with the nearby Glacier Skywalk for a fuller Columbia Icefield experience.

thingsToDoIntro: Jasper genuinely rewards a full day or two, split between its glacier, lakes and dark-sky nights.

thingsToDo.title: Boat to Spirit Island on Maligne Lake

image.alt: Boating to Spirit Island on Maligne Lake

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential Jasper experience, cruising the length of Maligne Lake to its famous island viewpoint.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book ahead in peak summer — tour slots do fill up.

thingsToDo.title: Walk on the Athabasca Glacier

image.file: File:Meltwater at the terminus of the Athabasca Glacier, Jasper National Park, Alberta, Canada.jpg
image.alt: The meltwater at the edge of the Athabasca Glacier

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rare opportunity, stepping onto real glacial ice on a guided walk or Ice Explorer tour.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely dress warmly — the ice keeps temperatures noticeably colder than the surrounding valley.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the Jasper SkyTram

image.file: File:Mount Edith Cavell from Sky Tram.jpg
image.alt: The view from the Jasper SkyTram

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely quick way to reach alpine terrain, with hiking trails continuing further up from the top station.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely go on a clear day — the summit view is the whole point.

thingsToDo.title: Hike the trail to Athabasca Falls

image.alt: Hiking the trail at Athabasca Falls

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely short, easy walk with a dramatic payoff, the river forcing itself through a narrow limestone gorge.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely stay behind the railings — the rocks here are slippery and the current is powerful.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the Maligne Canyon trail

image.alt: Walking the trail at Maligne Canyon

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding walk across a series of bridges spanning an increasingly deep limestone canyon.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely the first two bridges make a shorter loop if you're short on time.

thingsToDo.title: Swim or picnic at Pyramid Lake
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend an afternoon, swimming, paddling or simply picnicking by the water.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely the lake's small island is connected by a footbridge, worth the short walk across.

accommodation.intro: Jasper genuinely offers a smaller, more low-key range of lodging than Banff, from campgrounds to historic lodges.

areas.name: Jasper town
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely central, walkable and close to restaurants
areas.text: The most practical base, with easy access to the SkyTram and nearby trailheads.

areas.name: Along the Icefields Parkway
areas.bestFor: A genuinely more remote, scenic stay closer to the glacier
areas.text: A handful of lodges sit closer to the Columbia Icefield, useful for an early glacier start.

budget.label: Columbia Icefield Adventure (Ice Explorer and Skywalk)

gettingThere.intro: Jasper is genuinely reached either from Edmonton directly or via Banff along the Icefields Parkway.

options.text: Genuinely the most direct route, taking about four hours.
options.detail: A straightforward highway drive from Edmonton International Airport.

options.mode: Drive the Icefields Parkway from Banff
options.text: Genuinely the classic route, taking about three hours without stops.
options.detail: Budget a full day if combining the drive with sightseeing along the way.

options.mode: Via Rail's Jasper–Prince Rupert or Skeena route
options.text: Genuinely a scenic, if infrequent, rail option.
options.detail: Limited schedule, best for travellers building a slower, rail-focused trip.

gettingAround.intro: Jasper town is genuinely small and walkable, though a car is needed to properly explore the wider park.

options.text: Genuinely easy for the compact town centre.
options.detail: Restaurants, shops and the train station all sit within a short walk.

options.text: Genuinely essential for reaching Maligne Lake, the Athabasca Glacier and other key sights.
options.detail: Distances within the park are significant — plan driving time accordingly.

options.text: Genuinely a good option for the glacier and Maligne Lake if you'd rather not drive.
options.detail: Widely available, often including the Ice Explorer and boat tour together.

bestTime.headline: June to September for open roads and full glacier access
bestTime.summary: Jasper is genuinely a year-round destination, though most visitors come for the summer months when everything is accessible.

seasons.text: Genuinely the most reliable season, with every road, trail and glacier tour running.
Genuinely excellent, with fall colour and noticeably fewer visitors than summer.
Genuinely striking for stargazing and winter landscapes, though several attractions close for the season.
Genuinely a shoulder season, with snow lingering and some roads and trails still closed.

bestTime.avoid: Genuinely nothing strongly, though winter closes access to the Athabasca Glacier's Ice Explorer tours.

days.afternoon: Walk the bridges at Maligne Canyon.

days.title: The Athabasca Glacier

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Jasper visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely Maligne Lake boat tours and the Columbia Icefield Adventure ahead in peak summer.
Pack genuinely warm layers for the glacier — temperatures there run noticeably colder.
Carry genuinely bear spray for any hike beyond the busiest trails.
Check genuinely for a dark-sky event during your visit — Jasper's stargazing is genuinely exceptional.
Budget genuinely a full day for the Icefields Parkway drive from Banff, with stops.
Watch genuinely for wildlife on the roads, especially at dawn and dusk.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Jasper?
faq.a: Two to three days genuinely covers Maligne Lake, the Athabasca Glacier and the park's smaller sights comfortably.

faq.q: How does Jasper compare to Banff?
faq.a: Genuinely wilder and less crowded, with a larger park and more frequent wildlife sightings, at the cost of a longer drive from a major airport.

faq.q: Can you really walk on the Athabasca Glacier?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — via a guided walk or Ice Explorer vehicle tour, though independent access is genuinely dangerous due to crevasses.

faq.q: How do you get to Jasper?
faq.a: Genuinely easiest by driving from Edmonton, about four hours, or from Banff along the Icefields Parkway.
Yes, genuinely — it's one of the largest accessible dark sky preserves in the world, with regular public stargazing events.

faq.q: Can you combine Jasper with Banff?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — the Icefields Parkway between them is one of the most scenic drives in the world, and the natural way most visitors do both.
